paragraphs.text: IP based ACL gate for DeepSeek Harness
# dsh-ip-based-acl
A DeepSeek Harness plugin bundle that gates the Harness web surface by peer IP address.

> [!WARNING]
> **Early project, not security-reviewed.** This is 0.1.x: the tests drive a stub Conne

ction, the gate
> has never run against a live Harness, and nobody has audited it. Treat it as an ex

periment that
> works in the cases it tests, not as a boundary you can rely on — an address allowlis

t is one layer,
> never a substitute for a firewall, a TLS-terminating proxy, or a VPN.
>
> **Do not

expose DSH to the internet.** The Harness is powerful by design: it drives an agent with
> access t

o the machine it runs on, able to read and write files, execute commands, and reach the
> network. A

n instance reachable by someone you did not intend is, for practical purposes, remote code
> executi

on on that host. This bundle decides which peer addresses reach the door; it does not make
> public

exposure safe. Misconfiguration cuts both ways: an empty `allow` locks everyone out, and a
> `truste

dProxies` entry that covers real clients lets a forged `X-Forwarded-For` through. Run it on
> loopba

ck or behind a private network — VPN, WireGuard, Tailscale, an SSH tunnel — and keep it off the
> pu

private network — VPN, WireGuard, Tailscale, an SSH tunnel — and keep it off the
> public internet.

Status: **implemented, not installed**. The allowlist is compiled at activation and installed as a
g

ate over Connection's admission, index, and connect entries, with `X-Forwarded-For` resolution
throu

gh configured proxies. The bundle has not been installed into a live profile, so the gate has
not ye
t been exercised against a running Harness.
## Install
Node 24 or newer and pnpm are enough to build and test it: Cordis resolves from the Harness that loa

ds
the bundle at runtime, and from `devDependencies` for the local checks. `lib/` is generated rathe

r than
committed, so build before installing:

Install that directory as a **bundle** in a DSH profile — the Harness Plugin Manager's install actio

n,
or the `plugin_manager` tool with `action: install_bundle` and the checkout's absolute path as
`t
arget`. It contributes one Host row, `ip-based-acl`, and ships it without config.
Configure `allow` **before enabling the row**: the default is deny-everything, loopback included, so

a
row enabled with an empty list makes the web interface unreachable until you edit the profile pat

with an empty list makes the web interface unreachable until you edit the profile patch and
restart.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A manual install is the same package link the Plugin Manager makes:
`dsh plugin --profile <name> add
<path-to-this-checkout>`, which forwards `pnpm add` inside the profile.
## Policy
`allow` is an allowlist, and admission is default-deny.
- A client is admitted only when its address sits inside a configured address or CIDR network. A bar

e
address is a single-host rule (`203.0.113.9` is `/32`, `::1` is `/128`).
- A client that matches n

o entry is refused with `403`, even when it presents a valid launch token or
an existing session coo

kie.
- An empty `allow` list refuses every client, loopback included, and logs a warning at activati

on.
- A missing or unparseable client address is refused, never treated as local.
- A malformed patt

ern fails activation, so a typo cannot become a silent grant.
- IPv4 and IPv6 share one 128-bit spac

e: `10.0.0.0/8` and `::ffff:10.0.0.0/104` describe the same
peers, and a mapped peer matches either

spelling.
- Loopback must be listed explicitly (`127.0.0.1` and/or `::1`). A dual-stack listener oft

en reports
an IPv4 peer in mapped form (`::ffff:127.0.0.1`), which the IPv4 rule already covers.
## Proxies
`trustedProxies` names the reverse proxies whose `X-Forwarded-For` header may be believed. The chain
is resolved with MDN's trusted-proxy-list method:
- The socket peer is authoritative. If it is not in `trustedProxies`, it is the client and the heade

r
is ignored entirely — a direct client cannot spoof its way in.
- If it is, the list is read right

to left, starting with the address the nearest proxy recorded and
skipping every entry that is itsel

f a trusted proxy. The first entry that is not one is the client.
It may be an untrusted intermediat

e proxy rather than the origin, but it is the only address fit
for an access decision.
- Repeated `X

-Forwarded-For` headers form one chain. A malformed entry is treated as the client and
therefore ref

used.
- Name only proxies you control, never a client subnet: any host inside a trusted range can fo

rge the
header. A trusted proxy that sends no header falls back to its own address, so do not list a

proxy
in `allow` unless requests resolving to it should be admitted.
- The proxy must add `X-Forwar

ded-For` to the WebSocket upgrade as well as to plain HTTP requests.
An upgrade that arrives without

it resolves to the proxy's own address.
- An empty `trustedProxies` ignores the header, which is th

e safe default for a directly exposed
server.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Enforcement

The web carrier has no pre-dispatch hook and Connection exposes no policy extension point, so the
ga
te wraps the three entry points that decide whether a browser may use the interface:
| Entry point                   | Covers
| `connection.admit`            | every credential-bearing request: `/api`, the Remote-stream WebSoc

ket, and feature routes using `requestRejection` |
| `connection.authorizeIndex`   | the page itself

and the launch-token exchange                                                                   |
|
`connection.authorizeConnect` | the API credential exchange on `/connect`

An admitted peer continues through the normal token and cookie flow unchanged. A refused peer is
ans

wered before Connection reads the credential, so no token is exchanged, no cookie is minted, and a
c
ookie issued earlier buys nothing. Disposal restores every original method.
Scope limits, stated plainly:

- Public asset routes (plugin bundles, HMR events) stay reachable; they carry no session data, and
e

very data request behind them passes through `admit`.
- In-process peers (agent tools, workers) have

no socket address and never reach the gate.
